extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent representatives/attorneys, and KIPO examiners (users of the Korean Patent Act and Enforcement Rules)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules and standards for representation, calculation and extension of statutory/designated periods, invalidation and restoration of patent proceedings, and return of illegitimate application documents under the Korean Patent Act and its Enforcement Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of representation / subagent survivability
rubrics_metrics.description: The power of representation of a subagent in a patent-related proceeding shall not be extinguished in case of death of a representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference to the Patent Act and Civil Procedure Act mutatis mutandis; representative-subagent-principal relationships remain effective for ongoing proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple representatives — individual representation principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Where two or more representatives have been appointed, each of them shall independently represent the principal before KIPO or the Intellectual Property Trial and Appeal Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principle of individual representation applies among appointed representatives, between principal and appointed representative, between appointed representative and subagent, and for repeated proceedings by the same representative. Example: multiple representatives submitting amendments separately — all such amendments are deemed legitimately submitted; examiner should confirm which specification to examine per Part 5, Chap.3§6.3.1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proceedings by persons lacking capacity — ratification retroactivity
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent-related proceeding conducted by a person who lacks legal capacity, representation power, or authorization shall have effect retroactively to the time when such proceedings were performed if ratified by the principal upon gaining capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies where, e.g., the principal was a minor at time of proceeding but later attains legal capacity at 19 years old; proceedings by incompetent or unauthorized agents take effect retroactively upon ratification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint parties and common representative rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Where more than two parties jointly conduct a patent-related proceeding, each shall represent them all except for actions that could disadvantage other parties; if a common representative is appointed and notified to KIPO, only the common representative can conduct the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common representative(s) must submit evidential documents proving status and power of attorney (Annexed Form No.2 and Notification of Agent). Even a common representative cannot conduct proceedings under Article 11(1) without special powers from multiple parties; if common representative acts without such special power, KIPO will request amendment and may invalidate the proceeding if deficiencies are not addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: When only some parties appoint a representative
rubrics_metrics.description: If only some of the parties involved appoint a representative, the appointed representative can conduct patent-related proceedings on behalf of all, but must jointly conduct matters specified in Article 11(1) with the other parties involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a common representative does not represent all applicants, the representative's name must be specified appropriately in application forms (e.g., designate which applicant they represent in the Representative/Reference/Address fields).

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of periods — basic rules (Article 14)
rubrics_metrics.description: The first day of a period shall not be counted (except where the period commences at midnight); periods expressed in months or years are counted according to the calendar; if the starting day does not fall on the beginning day of a month/year the period expires on the day before the corresponding date in the last month/year; if no corresponding day exists in the last month, it expires on the last day of that month; if the last day falls on an official holiday (including Saturdays and designated Workers' Day), the period expires on the next working day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided (e.g., Lunar New Year holiday shifting expiry). Calculation primarily governed by Patent Act Article 14 with Civil Act Article 155 supplementing; natural vs calendar calculation differences explained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of certain statutory periods (Article 15(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Commissioner may extend the period for filing a petition for a trial under Article 132(17) only once by up to 30 days; number/period of extensions may be additionally increased for persons with poor transport access (islands/remote areas) as prescribed by Ordinance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions may be granted upon request or ex officio; special accommodations for disadvantaged locations per Ministry Ordinance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to shorten/extend designated periods and protect interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Commissioner, President of Trial and Appeal Board, presiding administrative patent judge, or an examiner may shorten or extend periods for patent-related proceedings upon request or ex officio; when doing so they must ensure interests of relevant parties are not unfairly infringed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a presiding judge specifies a deadline, they may change it upon request or ex officio.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of periods — statutory vs designated
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory periods are defined in the Patent Act or Orders under it; designated periods are set by KIPO officials (Commissioner, Board President, judge, examiner) pursuant to the Patent Act or Orders for a person filing an application or performing other patent-related proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List of statutory and designated periods relevant to examination (priority claim, request for examination, amendment periods, time for laying open, appeals, service by public announcement, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation specifics and holidays (notes/examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the last day of a period falls on a public holiday, the period expires the next working day; if calculation begins on a public holiday, the period starts from that public holiday; certain statutory/designated periods unrelated to patent proceedings are not extended by holidays (e.g., domestic priority withdrawal or patent term expiration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete example: amendment expiry January 27 falling on Lunar New Year leads to expiry Jan 29 after holiday/weekend; explanation of 'day on which calculation begins' vs 'expiration date'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic submission network glitches
rubrics_metrics.description: If a person intended to submit electronic documents but failed to deliver them within the period because of a network glitch, the period shall mature on the following day when the glitch is removed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Network glitch includes failure of computerized network or malfunction of computers/devices used in KIPO; not deemed a glitch if KIPO had previously notified of the network issue. Refer to Enforcement Rules Article 9(4) and KIPO announcements for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of Article 15-based expiration on calculation of extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: When a period is expired in accordance with Article 15 and the last day falls on a public holiday, the initial period matures on the public holiday and any extension is counted from the day after the expiration day; multiple extension requests are each calculated in this manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples and diagrams illustrate counting when months have no corresponding day and when extensions are counted from first day of month/year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of statutory periods — acceptance and process
rubrics_metrics.description: A statutory period for petition for appeal/trial can be extended once for up to thirty days; persons in poor transport areas can further extend; the President of the Trial and Appeal Board determines whether extension requirements are fulfilled and whether to accept the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative review by the Trial Policy Division; specific limits and discretionary determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of substantive examination designated periods — mechanics
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for extension under Enforcement Rules Article 16 can be filed for one month each time or for more than two months all at once; requests under one month are deemed one month; a request is generally deemed accepted when submitted except for the submission period for written argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners may approve only necessary time if third-party interests would be unlawfully infringed, and may disapprove remainder after warning. Rules for written-argument extension differ (see separate items).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of submission period for written argument — special rules and allowed reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: A request to extend the submission period for a written argument is deemed accepted if the desired extension expiry is within four months of the original expiry; if beyond that, examiner will examine reasons and may approve if necessary. Examiner may require explanation for additional extension requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerated acceptable reasons include: (①) new appointment/change of representative within 1 month before expiry; ② notification of change of applicant within 1 month before expiry limited to addition of a new applicant; ③ receipt of foreign office results and submission within 2 months before expiry; ④ delivery delayed over a month; ⑤ earlier or subsequent application pending in trial/lawsuit; ⑥ need for tests related to grounds for rejection; ⑦ other inevitable necessity. Requests related to third-party-filed applications may be disapproved even if matching reasons ①–⑤.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees and extension requests — payment requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If fees for a request for extension have not been paid, an examiner shall order an amendment within a designated period; if unpaid fees are paid within that designated period, the request is deemed legitimate; if fees are not paid within the designated period, the extension request is invalidated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guideline applies to statutory and designated periods regarding substantive and formality examinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Late submission of extension requests — examiner procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a request for extension of a designated period is submitted after expiration, the examiner shall give the applicant an opportunity to explain and return the request; the fees paid shall be returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a request is not approved, paid fees are returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of designated periods for formalities — limits and acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: Extension of amendment periods under Article 46 can be requested in one-month increments or multiple months; the total period allowed for extension is four months in general, with additional exceptions for international national phase entries; when total requested extension does not exceed four months and fees are paid, the request is deemed approved upon submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the requested period reaches four months, examiner must state in approval that 'any further extension shall not be allowed' and notify applicant; further requests will be disapproved. Late requests after expiry are returned and fees refunded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shortening of designated periods (applicant request)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a designated period has been set, it can be shortened upon request; when a request or an amendment indicating intent to shorten is submitted, the designated period is deemed expired on the day of submission and the examiner shall carry out the examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to expedite examination by applicant request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order to amend and grounds (Article 46)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commissioner or President of the Trial and Appeal Board shall order a relevant person to amend a patent-related proceeding within a specified period in cases such as violations of Article 3(1) or 6, violations of any formality specified in the Act or orders thereunder, or failure to pay any fee required under Article 82.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The person ordered may submit an argument on the order during the specified period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidation of proceeding for failure to amend (Article 16)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a person ordered under Article 46 fails to amend within the specified period, the Commissioner or the President of the Trial and Appeal Board may invalidate the patent-related proceeding. If failure to pay fees caused the issue, the amendment to the specification accompanying the patent application may be invalidated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If invalidated but failure was due to cause not attributable to the person ordered, invalidation may be revoked upon request within two months after cause ceases, except where one year has passed since expiration of specified period. Notice must be given when invalidation or revocation occurs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsequent completion of proceedings (Article 17)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a person failed to complete a patent-related proceeding within the period due to a cause not attributable to them, they may subsequently complete the proceeding within 2 months after the cause ceases, except where one year has passed since expiration of the specified period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies specifically to filing petition for trial under Article 132-17 and petition for retrial under Article 180(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration of patent application (Article 67-3)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application was withdrawn or a decision to reject became final due to the applicant's failure to comply with time limits caused by reasons not attributable to the applicant, the applicant may request examination or re-examination within two months from the date the cause ceases, except where one year has elapsed since the period expired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant periods include request for examination under Article 59(2)/(3) and re-examination under Article 67-2(1). If filed, the application is deemed not withdrawn or the decision deemed not final and conclusive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return / non-acceptance of illegitimate application documents (Enforcement Rules Article 11)
rubrics_metrics.description: KIPO shall not deem certain application documents legitimate (and will return them) where they fall under specified subparagraphs, including form violations, unclear application type, missing name or applicant code, not written in Korean, missing specification, missing claims when amendment period elapsed, submission by person without domicile/place of business in Korea (except patent administrator), submissions not within designated period, requests for extension for non-extendable periods, requests submitted after certain expiries, documents submitted after termination of proceeding, submissions by persons not entitled, unclear/invalid annexed documents (specific annex forms), or electronic submissions not using KIPO software or in an unprocessable form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists many concrete grounds (numbered 1–13-2 in the Enforcement Rules excerpt) and notes fees/processing implications; KIPO will return or not accept such documents except where special provisions apply.
